source_pack.canonical_content_text:
Meta's Muse AI agent achieves strong growth, company introduces new shares to power investments

Meta will issue a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January ​2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control amid Silicon Valley's intensifying AI ​race.

The company raised the lower end of its annual spending forecast, now expecting capital expenditure to be between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from $130 billion to $145 billion expected previously.

The company reported better-than-expected revenue of $64.60 billion for the quarter ended September 30, ahead of Wall Street estimates of $63.37 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Meta reported a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive free cash ​flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier.
